newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end slightly higher, still bullish.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end slightly higher, still bullish.

text.p: French shares closed firmer, rebounding from their morning consolidation.

Traders said strength in bonds and hopes of interest rate cuts in France and Germany as early as this week gave reasons to be cheerful for Paris equities, which shrugged off a decline on Wall Street. Hopes are also high for big flows from cash-rich U.S. funds in the New Year, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.97 points or 0.13 percent at 2,318.63 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,322 from 2,319 on Friday's close.
* Pension funds are picking blue chips for year-end window-dressing of books, adding to CAC index gains.
* Legrand up 1.1 percent at 915 francs, L'Oreal up 0.73 percent at 1,925, LVMH up 0.83 percent at 1,335 among those benefitting.

* Lyonnaise des Eaux firms 1.77 percent to 506. A major French broker said a market news service reported that a big domestic bank downgraded the stock to reduce from add and that Lyonnaise could merge with Tractebel of Belgium through a share swap. Lyonnaise officials were not available for comment.

* Cie Bancaire continues climbing, up 2.36 percent at 608 francs. Its Cetelem subsidiary "has performed very well, Bancaire has a lot of catching up to do," said one senior equity salesman. Cetelem was down 0.55 percent at 1,255 on rumours of share sales, after a recent substantial rise.

* Renault, falls 3.31 percent to 119.90, while PSA Peugeot Citroen eases 0.62 percent to 638. Both were hit by November car sales figures which showed a 21.7 percent drop, following the end of the state rebate for new cars. Investors switched into Michelin, which rose 1.31 percent to 271.40.

* Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere ease respectively 1.64 percent to 467 francs and 0.32 percent to 157.5. Uncertainties over the Thomson privatisation weigh, as well as GEC Plc's demands on Alcatel for an equal share in the Framatome proposed merger.
* Eurotunnel drops 6.9 percent to 6.75 francs, still under pressure from the disturbance of its passenger service since a fire two weeks ago.
